thread.title: Apple surges to lead Silicon Valley stocks higher as markets rebound

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Apple surges to lead Silicon Valley stocks higher as markets rebound

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high tech index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 12, 2018, 1:38pm PST Updated Feb 12, 2018, 1:40pm PST The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index roared out of the gate on Monday after a rollercoaster week for the stock market. The region's stocks were swept up by the broader stock market, which moved back into positive territory on Monday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 410 points and the S&P 500 gained 1.39 percent on Monday. Bloomberg's index of Silicon Valley's largest technology stocks gained 2.42 percent, led by Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). The Cupertino-based iPhone maker jumped 4.02 percent. Earlier, Goldman Sachs predicted that the iPhone maker, flush with cash it plans to bring back from overseas, could mount a major acquisition . Apple was followed by chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), up 3.32 percent. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) gained 2.89 percent. Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) surged 2.74 percent, followed by Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE), up 2.15 percent. All 13 of the stocks on the index closed up Monday. The worst performers were Facebook (NASDAQ: FB), Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL) and Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), up 0.01 percent, 0.84 percent and 0.85 percent, respectively. Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the biggest gainers Monday: • Trimble (NASDAQ: TRMB) jumped 5.07 percent. The Sunnyvale-based electronics manufacturer last week reported fourth-quarter earnings that beat analyst expectations . • Arista Networks (NASDAQ: NYSE: ANET) gained 4.4 percent. • Lam Research Corp. (NASDAQ: LRCX) gained 4.27 percent. The worst performers among all Silicon Valley stocks: • San Mateo-based action camera maker GoPro (NASDAQ: GPRO) dropped 3.66 percent. • Infinera Corp. (NASDAQ: INFN) fell 2.57 percent. • Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) slumped 1.75 percent after leading local stocks on Friday on a blockbuster earnings beat. Ranked by Local employee headcount Rank
